page: Microsoft Azure DC96as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The configuration provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation totals 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache distribution includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core block. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring deployment with network-attached storage volumes, and it supports Premium Storage. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero discrete GPUs attached. Benchmark evaluations place the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance in the top 25 percent with a score of 110477.48, while stress-ng single-core performance registers at 2022.45, positioning it within the middle 50 percent tier. In-memory data handling demonstrates high throughput, achieving 91.95 million operations per second on redis SET operations, which also falls into the top 25 percent tier.

With its dense 96-thread execution capacity and balanced memory allocation, the DC96as_v5 provides scalable throughput for multi-threaded enterprise workloads. Cost efficiency derives from high CPU core density and strong multi-core scaling relative to general-purpose cloud allocations, though workloads requiring ultra-fast local scratch disks or AVX-512 vector acceleration must accommodate remote storage latency and standard vector limits. Suitable workloads include large-scale web backends, distributed memory caches, relational database systems, batch processing, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure DC96as_v5 is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine includes 384.0 GB of memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU. It operates without integrated local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on Premium Storage remote disks for persistent data. Hardware extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic support. Synthetic benchmarks reflect strong performance, with stress-ng multi-core results reaching 110477.48 and redis SET operations processing 91.95 million operations per second, both ranking in the top 25 percent tier. Single-core performance falls in the middle 50 percent tier with a stress-ng score of 2022.45. This configuration fits high-concurrency enterprise workloads including distributed caching, transactional databases, batch processing pipelines, and multi-tier enterprise application servers requiring broad multi-threaded CPU capacity.
